source.declaration: All Task 9 release gates and retained-artifact scans ran from a clean worktree at the source commit. This manifest, the human report, and the README/PLAN/TASKS evidence updates were written afterward and are not part of the source commit under test.

release_gates.command: uv --directory apps/api run ruff check app tests ../../evals

release_gates.claim_boundary: Asset and layout-foundation gate only; not visual proof.

warnings: Next.js emitted the existing multiple-lockfile workspace-root inference warning.

release_gates.duration_observation: less than 0.01 seconds at the timer's 0.01-second display resolution

release_gates.skip_policy: All 31 skips are explicit project or opt-in-capture routing; no failure was converted to a skip.

formal_browser_evidence.capture_source: Task 8 Fix Round 3 formal production capture on the same final source tree; Task 9 rechecked file identity and dimensions without rewriting the owned screenshot files.

artifact_and_privacy_checks.limitation: Field names and privacy-rejection fixtures remain in source by design; the zero-match claim applies to retained artifacts and credential-shaped value assignments, not to schema identifiers or labeled synthetic test constants.

verification_history.note: The first full release run was green, but a later finishing rerun exposed a readiness race, so this result was not accepted as final stability evidence.

verification_history.disposition: Task 9 stopped and routed the non-owned E2E readiness race to Task 8.

verification_history.interleaved_stability: 150 passed, 0 failed across the two newly exposed scenarios and reduced-motion focus path

known_limitations: The product, brand, creator, content, comment, price, inventory, and cart data are frozen synthetic fixtures.
No real LLM, embedding model, vector index, Hybrid RAG, reranker, or LLM judge is used.
The 6/6 evaluation result applies only to six frozen deterministic cases and is not a real recommendation-quality score.
Browser evidence is local Chromium only. It is not cross-browser certification, a user study, or production reliability evidence.
The in-memory Guide session does not survive an API process restart and provides no production authentication or durable persistence model.
No conversion, trust, task-completion, latency, cost, uptime, business-impact, payment, order, or fulfillment claim is supported.
The idempotency key remains in the reconciliation URL; local evidence disables access logs, but productionization must prevent proxy or access-log retention.
Next.js still emits the known multiple-lockfile workspace-root warning, and dev E2E still emits the known one-dimension image warning.
